name: 2016 Calumet Avenue — Brick dwelling (district draft; refined by T-1946)

function.note: The 1911 sheet marks the building 'D' (dwelling): '3B brick dwelling (D) faced in stone (blue) along its Calumet front, with a canted bay there, and a 2B rear part'. Carried to 1904 on the T-3018 census ruling (present_as_mapped).

research_note: A DISTRICT DRAFT (T-3018, the owner's district pass of 2026-10-08): a serviceable first model, complete from the street, the walks, the alley and the air, that T-1946 refines in place under this same id. Written by tools/draft_prairie_1904.py from the sheet 35e trace (s35efp-calumet_2016-b1), the T-3018 census (s35e-2016-front) and the T-1837 register row frontage-35e-2016 (Brick dwelling); every height, roof, opening and feature is the draft rules' reconstruction (data/components/prairie_1904/draft_prairie_1904.json; liberty L-draft-district-background-3018).

documented_range.note: The draft claims the 1904 target and no more: the 1911 sheet draws the building and the T-3018 census rules it present in 1904 (present_as_mapped). Its building and loss dates are the per-building ticket's to read.

position.symbolic_location: 2016 S. Calumet Avenue, parcel calumet_2016 (data/street_grid/1904.json), west side of Calumet Avenue, the background behind Prairie Avenue: Calumet Avenue's west frontage, 20th to 22nd Street, beside the named Hanford and Wheeler-Kohn houses (Sanborn 1911 vol. 3 sheet 35).
position.note: The rear corner of the main body's rectangle (lot frame u 32.500, v -3.000 m from the middle of the rear lot line), through the T-1250 fit of the sheet: the sheet's georeference carries no independent check: its own fit residual is 0.05 m RMS on its control crossings, a similarity on two degrees of freedom that says little away from them, plus about a pixel (0.19 m) of trace on this coarser copy. Rotation -0.621 degrees turns the plan's u axis onto the lot's own rear-to-street line.

derivation.reason: The four derivation methods re-derive from the 1835 files; this position is re-derived from the traced sheet and the 1904 parcel by tools/draft_prairie_1904.py --check instead.

footprint.note: The main body: the largest rectangle that fits inside the traced main part (u toward the street, v along the front), widened to 5.5 m along the front because the fitted strip was narrower than any house of the avenue (T-2690). The building's other rectangles are in draft_plan.

stories.note: '3B; rear2B' printed on the 1911 sheet: 3 full storeys.

Storeys per piece and roof per piece are the draft rules' (reconstructed).

draft_elevation.note: RECONSTRUCTED by the draft rules, family row '(default)' overlaid with the frontage row: A background house with no named record and no register row: the brick family's hip over the sheet's printed storeys, every face closed, nothing read beyond the sheet. 3B behind a stone face on the Calumet front, its 2B rear part as printed. No Prairie stand sees this lot (the census's 0 stands); it is drafted so the frontage stands whole. Heights are the rules' starting values inside RECONSTRUCTION-RULES.md's ranges; bays, entrance side, chimneys and dormers are counts the family rules choose, and the seed 3146765073 only tints the fabric inside +-6 %.
